---
title: "Compile a query"
subtitle: "Ship a query as a small native program"
execute:
  enabled: false
---

Write a query once, in Mojo, and mark the values that change between runs with
`param()`. `marrow compile` turns it into a native executable in which every
parameter is a command-line flag, so one binary answers the same question for
any file and any threshold, with no Python and no interpreter behind it.

::: {.callout-note}
The code on this page is Mojo, compiled ahead of time. For queries built at run
time from Python, see [Lazy queries](queries-lazy.qmd).
:::

## Why compile a query

- **The query is the program.** Column types are fixed when the query is
  compiled, so `col("amount", int64) >= param("min-amount", int64)` fuses into a
  single loop, and the executable links the kernels this query uses and nothing
  else. The example below is 3.0 MB of machine code.
- **Far smaller than an interpreter.** The same `GROUP BY` compiled this way is
  1.45 MB of machine code; resolving its aggregates by name at run time, as a
  dynamic frontend must, takes 13.2 MB, **9.1× as much**. See
  [why the compiled binary is small](../reference/architecture.qmd#why-the-compiled-binary-is-small).
- **Values change, code does not.** Parameters are read when the program starts,
  so a daily report is one binary run against a different file and threshold
  each day.
- **A command line for free.** `--help`, `--describe`, output formats and error
  messages come from the query itself; there is no argument parsing to write.
- **Easy to ship.** `--bundle` gathers the executable and the libraries it loads
  into one directory that runs without pixi or a marrow install.

## When to use it

Compile a query whose shape is settled and that runs many times: a report, an
export, a filter in a data pipeline. A query you are still shaping belongs in
[Python](queries-lazy.qmd), where changing it is a line rather than a rebuild —
**a build takes a minute or two**, because the whole library is compiled at
`-O3` each time.

## Write the query

```{.mojo filename="benchmarks/binary_size/query_cli.mojo"}
{{< include ../../benchmarks/binary_size/query_cli.mojo >}}
```

- `query()` builds the plan. It is a function because Mojo has no module-level
  variables.
- `param(name, dtype)` is a value supplied at run time, and the input file is
  one too: `scan(param("src", string), ...)`.
- `QueryCli(query()).run()` is the whole program: every `param` in the plan
  becomes a `--name` flag.

## Build it

```bash
$ marrow compile query_cli.mojo -o orders
```

In a marrow checkout, where the `marrow` script is not installed, run the same
command as `pixi run python -P python/marrow/compile.py compile query_cli.mojo
-o orders`. Add `--fast` for a quicker `-O1` build of a slower program, and
`-v` to see the underlying `mojo build` command.

## Run it

The flags come from the plan, typed by the parameters' dtypes:

```bash
$ ./orders --help
usage: ./orders [-h] --src string --min-amount int64 [--describe] [--output PATH] [--format FMT] [--max-rows N]

options:
  -h, --help              show this help message
      --src string        (required)
      --min-amount int64  (required)
      --describe          print the query plan and exit
  -o, --output PATH       write results here (default: stdout)
      --format FMT        output format: table | csv | parquet | ipc (default: inferred from --output's extension, else table)
      --max-rows N        rows to print for `table` output, 0 for all (default: 20)
```

Against a seven-row `orders.parquet` whose `amount` column is
`[100, 250, 90, 1000, 250, null, 42]`:

```bash
$ ./orders --src orders.parquet --min-amount 250
id  amount  name
--  ------  ----
2   250     bob
4   1000    dave
5   250     erin
(3 rows)
```

`--describe` prints the plan baked into the binary, and needs no other
arguments:

```bash
$ ./orders --describe
Filter(ParquetScan(param(src)), greater_equal(col(amount), param(min-amount)))
```

A mistake on the command line prints the usage and exits with status 2; a
failure while running exits with status 1. Both go to stderr:

```bash
$ ./orders --src orders.parquet --min-amount abc
usage: ./orders [-h] --src string --min-amount int64 [--describe] [--output PATH] [--format FMT] [--max-rows N]
./orders: error: --min-amount: expected int64, got 'abc'
```

## Output

The default is an aligned table, capped at `--max-rows`. `--format csv` writes
RFC 4180 CSV and is never truncated, so it is safe to pipe:

```bash
$ ./orders --src orders.parquet --min-amount 250 --format csv
id,amount,name
2,250,bob
4,1000,dave
5,250,erin
```

`-o PATH` writes to a file and picks the format from its extension: `.csv`,
`.parquet` or `.pq`, `.arrow` or `.ipc`. Parquet and Arrow IPC output are
opt-in, because their writers add about 700 KB of machine code that a program
which only prints should not carry:

```{.mojo .fragment}
QueryCli(query()).run[parquet=True, ipc=True]()
```

## Parameters

A parameter is required unless it has a default, and `help=` gives it a line in
`--help`; `description=` sets the program's own:

```{.mojo .fragment}
param("min-amount", int64, default=Int64(0), help="keep orders at or above this")
QueryCli(query(), description="Orders at or above a minimum amount.").run()
```

| dtype | on the command line |
|---|---|
| integers | `250`, `-3` — refused if the type cannot hold the value |
| floats | `0.25`, `1e-3` |
| `bool` | `true`, `false`, `1`, `0` |
| `string`, `large_string` | any text |

Parameters of other types appear in `--help` but cannot be set from the command
line yet, so they need a default. A name used twice in a plan is one parameter
and one flag.

## Skip what the filter rules out

Optimize the plan with `ScanPruning` and the scan reads only the row groups and
pages whose statistics could hold a matching row — thresholds from the command
line included:

```{.mojo .fragment}
QueryCli(query().optimize[ScanPruning]()).run()
```

```bash
$ ./orders --describe
Filter(ParquetScan(param(src)) pruned by 1, greater_equal(col(amount), param(min-amount)))
```

It links the optimizer, which adds about 1.5 MB of machine code to this example,
so it pays off for large files rather than small ones.

## Ship it

A compiled executable loads the Mojo runtime libraries from the environment it
was built in. `--bundle DIR` copies the executable, those libraries and marrow's
Parquet compression codecs into one directory:

```bash
$ marrow compile query_cli.mojo -o orders --bundle dist
$ zip -ry orders.zip dist        # -y keeps the bundle's symlinks
```

`dist/orders` then runs from any directory with no pixi environment and no
marrow install; copy the directory to a machine with the same OS and CPU
architecture. The object-store backend is not bundled, so a bundle reads local
files.

## Limits worth knowing

- The plan's shape is fixed at compile time; only parameter values change per
  run.
- Column names are checked when the program runs, not when it compiles.
- There is no incremental build: every compile takes a minute or two.
- A bundle is checked on the machine that built it. The brotli codec's own
  dependency is found the way it was at build time, so brotli-compressed files
  are the least certain case elsewhere.
- `marrow compile` has no `-D` passthrough, so a GPU build
  (`-D MARROW_GPU=true`) needs `mojo build` directly.
